title: Noscitur a sociis: reading a word with its companions
shortTitle: Noscitur a sociis: reading a word with its companions
summary: This associated-words canon uses neighboring terms to identify the relevant sense or scope of an ambiguous word.
notes:
The inference works when the surrounding words supply a meaningful common category. In Raila and Dolan, loss and miscarriage suggested failures involving delivery of mail, which narrowed negligent transmission. Reading transmission as every act during delivery would reach much farther than its neighbors.

The canon does not mechanically require the narrowest possible meaning, and other text can defeat the proposed category. It also differs from ejusdem generis, which concerns general language following a list of more specific items. Katzmann’s drafting discussion observes that staff can follow associated-word reasoning without knowing its Latin name, a reason to ask whether a canon reflects ordinary drafting practice.
